- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >3%), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above true value to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is ambiguous (0.33–0.67).
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00), model lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 75% of 30-day moving average, model often misses downward trend; apply a 1–3% downward bias to prevent underestimation.
